FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Automotive Electrical Equipment and Instruments Sectional Committee and approval of the Transport 
Engineering Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1993. This revision ofthe standard includes electronic type of pressure gauges 
besides temperature resistance test and specifies cold test. 


Electrical/electronic type pressure gauges are useful for indicating the pressure developed in an automotive 
engine system. 


In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) J 1810 : 2010 
“Electrical indicating system specification”. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules 
for rounding off numerical values (revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value 
should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3 TYPES AND CLASSES 


Class 1 Coil type — Variable resistance type sender 
unit 

Class 2 Stepper motor — Variable resistance type 
sender unit 


4 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 The construction of gauges shall be as shown in 
Fig. 1. 
4.2 The gauge shall comprise of unitized sender and 


receiver units. The sender unit converts the pressure 
and the receiver unit indicates it. 


4.3 The graduation shall be in kPa or bar. Additional 
graduation in kg/cm? may be provided. The gauges shall 
be plated or painted. Arrangements for illumination 


lines 
shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the 
purchaser.

5 SAMPLING 


Unless otherwise agreed upon, the sampling plan shall 
be in accordance with IS 2500 (Part 1). 


6 TESTS 


6.1 Test Conditions 
The test conditions shall be as follows: 


a) Temperature and humidity, at the test place, shall 
be kept constant in the specified error tests, the 
temperature shall be 15 to 35°C and humidity 
shall be 45-75 percent. 


b) Mounting condition shall be determined on the 
kind of vehicles. 


c) Pressure gauge with an accuracy of + 0.25 percent 
of full scale range shall be used for the pressure 
measurement. 


d) Test voltage shall be as shown in Table 1. 


e) In the indication error test, tapping of the receiver 
unit to be done to remove influence of any 
frictional resistance. 


f) Ohm meter least count shall be 0.1 Q or less. 


Table 1 Test Voltages 
[Clause 6.1(d)] 


SI Nominal Performance Test Endurance Test 
No. Voltage Voltage in Volts Voltage in Volts 
(1) (2) (3) (4) 

i) 12 13.5 14+0.5 
ii) 24 27.0 28+1.0 


6.2 Indication Error Test 


Indication error of gauges shall be as shown in Table 2. 


6.3 Delay of Indication 


The response time of the gauge for sudden change of 
pressure shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer 
and the user. 


6.4 Insulation Resistance 


At 500 V dc the insulation resistance, between the 
receiver unit terminal and outer case shall be more than 
one mega ohm. This is applicable for insulated type 
meter only. 


6.5 High Voltage (Flash) Test 


When the receiver unit of the gauge is subjected to 
a flash test at 500 V a.c. rms at a frequency of 40 to 
60 Hz between the gauge terminals and outer case, it 
shall satisfactorily withstand the test without arcing or 
puncture. This is applicable for insulated type meter 
only. 


IS 13646 : 2018 


6.6 Damp Heat (Cyclic) Test 


When the receiver unit of the gauge is subjected for damp 
heat (cyclic) test according to IS 9000 (Part 5/Sec 2) 
and the number of conditioning cycles is two, each part 
shall be free from any abnormalities and the permissible 
variation between the observed value and the initial 
value shall be + 2 percent of full scale value. 


6.7 Vibration Resistance 


When the gauge is subjected to vibration resistance, 
as specified in IS 9000 (Part 8), the receiver unit and 
the sending unit shall be capable of withstanding 
18 h of vibration, 6 h along each of the three mutually 
perpendicular axes. One axes is to be perpendicular to 
the mounting plane. The vibration test shall be run at 
double amplitude or acceleration listed in Table 3 with 
a frequency sweep through the range of 10-2 000-10 Hz 
at a rate of one octave per minute (15.3 min per 
sweep). The test shall be run at room temperature. 
A nominal sending unit load for mid-scale pointer 
position shall be applied to the receiver unit. Sending 
units shall be run at 50 percent of full scale measured 
parameter and for this purpose shall be loaded with a 
suitable receiver unit. During the test run of either a 
receiver unit or a sending unit, the receiver unit pointer 
motion shall show no signs of electrical shorting or 
loss of electrical continuity. The permissible variation 
of the observed values from the initial values shall be 
+ 2 percent of full scale value. No abnormalities shall 
be observed in other parts. The receiver and sender unit 
shall be tested separately.

6.8 Endurance Test 6.12 Temperature Resistance 
The receiver unit shall be connected with the sender When the gauge is tested as specified in 


unit and pressure to the sender unit from the lowest 
graduation pressure to 80 percent of the highest 
graduation pressure shall be applied and then reduced 
to lowest graduation pressure. This process at the 
rate of 10 to 30 cycle/min for 1 00 000 times shall be 
repeated. The permissible variation of the observed 
values from the initial values shall be + 2 percent of the 
full scale value. No abnormalities shall be observed in 
other parts. 


NOTE — In case of oil pressure sender unit, oil shall be used 
as a medium and temperature shall be 100 + 5°C. In case of air 
pressure sender unit, air shall be used as a medium. 


6.9 Water Spray Test 


When the gauge is tested as per IS 9000 (Part 16), 
exposing only the front parts for 2 h. All the opening 
shall be suitably sealed except in case of waterproof 
gauge. After test, there shall be no visible entry of water 
inside the gauge and also the permissible variation 
between the observed values from the initial value shall 
be + 2 percent of full scale value. 


6.10 Salt Spray Test 


When the gauge is tested as per IS 9000 (Part 11) for 
50 h consisting of two periods, each period being of 
24 h of spraying and 1 hour draining. After test, the 
gauge shall be subjected to the high voltage flash test 
(This is applicable for insulated type meter only) and 
the permissible variation of the observed values from 
the initial values shall be + 2 percent of full scale value. 
The visual appearance of the gauge after the test shall 
not be considered for declaring failure of sample. 


6.11 Dust Test 


When the receiver unit of the gauge is tested as per 
IS 9000 (Part 12) for 5 h. All the opening shall be 
suitably sealed except in case of dust proof gauge. After 
test, there shall be no visible entry of dust inside the 
gauge and also the permissible variation ofthe observed 
values from the initial values shall be + 2 percent of full 
scale value. 


IS 9000 (Part 14/Sec 2), each part shall be free from any 
abnormalities and the permissible variation between 
the observed value from the initial value shall be 
+ 2 percent of full scale value. 


6.13 Cold Test 


When the gauge is tested as specified in 
IS 9000 (Part 2/Sec 3) with a gradual change of 
temperature under the following conditions: 

E 3°C; 

b) Duration of exposure 2 h; and 


a) Temperature 10 4 


c) After the test, the permissible variation between 
the observed values, from the initial value shall be 


within + 2 percent of full scale value. 
6.14 Dry Heat Test 
When the gauge is tested as specified in 


IS 9000 (Part 3/Sec 3) with a gradual change of 

temperature under the following conditions: 

E 2°C; 

b) Duration of exposure : 4 h; and 

c) After the test the gauge shall be cooled to the 
ambient temperature of 15 to 35°C and visually 
examined for any defects. The permissible 
variation of the observed values from the initial 
values after the test shall be + 2 percent of full 
scale value. 


6.15 Drop Test 


After testing the gauge as per IS 9000 (Part 7/Sec 3), 
the permissible variation of the observed values from 
the initial values after the test shall be + 2 percent of 
full scale value. 


a) Temperature : 70 4 


6.16 Bump Test 


After testing the gauge as per IS 9000 (Part 7/Sec 2) 
the permissible variation between the observed and the 
initial values shall not exceed + 2 percent of full scale 
value. 


6.17 Additional Testing Exclusive to Sending Unit 


6.17.1 Burst Pressure Test 


Sender unit of the gauge is subjected to three times 
highest graduation pressure, and is applied for a period 
of 1 min. There shall be no leakage during the test. 


6.17.2 Sealing Test with Drilled Diaphragm 


A hole of 1.5 mm diameter is drilled in the diaphragm. 
The sender unit is then mounted in normal position 
of use and subjected to a pressure of 10 kg/cm? for 
2 min with SAE 40 oil at 120 + 2°C. There shall be no 
leakage during the test. 


6.18 Additional Testing Exclusive to Electronic 
Pressure Gauge 


6.18.1 Power Source Reverse Connecting Test 


As to receiver unit for nominal voltage 12 V connect 
the test voltage of 13.0 V, for 24 V, the test voltage 
of 26 V with the reverse electrode for 1 min. After 
the test, sample shall be examined for the existence 
of abnormalities and the permissible variation of 
the observed values from the initial values shall be 
+ 2 percent of full scale value. 


6.18.2 Over Voltage Test 


The test to over voltage of receiver unit shall be in 
accordance with the following. 


6.18.2.1 Over voltage test (long duration test) 


For receiver unit of nominal voltage 12 V, apply 
the test voltage of 18 V, for of 24 V apply 36 V and 
after actuating for 1 hour, examine for existence of 
abnormalities of each part. 


6.18.2.2 Over voltage test (short duration test) 


For receiver unit of nominal voltage 12 V, apply the 
test voltage of 24 V, for 24 V apply 48 V, for 1 min and 
thereafter, examine the existence of abnormalities for 
each part. 


IS 13646 : 2018 


6.18.3 Transient Voltage Test 


The receiver unit shall comply with requirements of 
ISO 7637-2 and ISO 7637-3. 


6.18.4 Electromagnetic Compatibility Test 


As agreed to between the manufacturer and the user, 
the receiver unit of the gauge shall meet statutory 
electromagnetic compatibility requirements. 


7 MARKING 


7.1 Each gauge shall have the following information 
marked preferably on the dial or on a name plate in a 
permanent and legible manner in a location where it is 
accessible and visible. 


a) Name and address of manufacturer; 

b) Symbol of gauge; 

c) Serial number indication of the source of 
manufacturer; 

d) Trade or brand name; and 

e) Date of manufacturing. 


7.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


7.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of the conditions under which the licence for 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
“BIS Catalogue’ and “Standards: Monthly Additions’.
